c: Tidewater Realty, a residential real estate brokerage with 35 agents
s: Tidewater Realty's agents use personal phones and email accounts to share client documents, including mortgage pre-approvals and photo IDs. Last month an agent's phone was stolen and a client's identity information was exposed.
The managing broker (judge) has asked you and your partner to analyze the situation and recommend what the brokerage must do now and how to prevent future problems.
f: 35 agents, 600 active clients
No written policy on handling client data
Two clients have asked whether the brokerage is legally responsible
A competitor advertises 'bank-level data security'
p: Describe legal issues affecting businesses
Explain information privacy, security, and confidentiality considerations in business
Comply with the spirit and intent of laws and regulations
Explain the role of ethics in information management
Recognize and respond to ethical dilemmas
n: Notifies affected clients promptly and explains what happened
Names breach-notification duties and potential liability for negligence
Writes a data policy: encryption, approved storage, remote wipe, training
Explains that ethical duty goes beyond legal minimums
Offers support such as credit monitoring and a point of contact
q: Should the brokerage tell clients before it knows the full extent of the breach? Why?
What would you do if an agent refused to follow the new policy?

c: Skyline Gym Group, a chain of fitness centers
s: Skyline Gym Group sells memberships through an online form. Many members report they could not cancel without visiting a location in person, and some say they were charged after they believed they had canceled. Two states are reviewing the gym's practices.
The chief operating officer (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the company's exposure and recommend changes to its contracts and cancellation process.
f: 22,000 members, 18 locations
Cancellation requires in-person visit with signed form
Monthly refunds for disputed charges average $18,000
State consumer protection offices opened inquiries
p: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts
Describe legal issues affecting businesses
Explain legal and ethical considerations in selling
Handle customer/client complaints
Explain the role of ethics in customer relationship management
n: Explains that contract terms must be clear, fair and not deceptive
Identifies consumer protection laws and regulatory risk
Recommends easy online cancellation, clear fees and written confirmation
Describes a complaint process and refunds for wrongful charges
Weighs short-term revenue against long-term trust
q: How much revenue might the gym lose if it makes cancellation easy, and why is it worth it?
What would you say to a member who says they were misled?

c: Parker & Quinn Design, a small design studio owned by two friends
s: Parker & Quinn Design has grown from two friends to eight employees. The founders disagree about who makes decisions, profit is split informally, and one founder wants to leave and take a major client.
The owner (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the business structure and recommend how to protect the company and the clients.
f: Operating as a general partnership with no written agreement
Annual revenue $640,000
One client is 30% of revenue
Founder A wants to start a competing studio
p: Explain types of business ownership
Explain the nature of agency relationships
Describe the nature of legally binding contracts
Describe methods used to protect intellectual property
Take responsibility for decisions and actions
n: Compares partnership with LLC and corporation: liability, taxes, control
Explains that each partner can bind the firm and be personally liable
Recommends a partnership or operating agreement, non-compete and buy-sell terms
Clarifies who owns designs and client relationships
Recommends a plan to retain the client and communicate transparently
q: How would you value the studio if one founder left?
Would you recommend an LLC? Why or why not?

c: Beacon Learning, an online tutoring company
s: Beacon Learning allows tutors to record sessions and keeps them for quality review. A parent has asked for all recordings of her 14-year-old to be deleted. The company's policy is unclear and tutors sometimes share clips on social media for marketing.
The chief executive officer (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how the company should manage recordings and student information.
f: 8,000 student accounts, 400 tutors
Recordings stored indefinitely
Marketing team used five student clips last month
No policy on parental consent
p: Explain legal issues associated with information management
Explain the role of ethics in information management
Maintain data security
Respect the privacy of others
Explain ethical considerations in providing information
n: Recognizes extra protections for minors' information
Gets clear consent before recording or sharing clips
Sets retention limits and deletion on request
Restricts access and trains tutors and marketers
Balances business needs with student privacy
q: Should the company continue to use student clips in marketing if parents consent? Why?
What would you do if a tutor shared a clip without permission?

c: Redline Motors, a car dealership group
s: A Redline Motors salesperson sold a used car without telling the buyer it had been in a flood. A mechanic reported it to the manager, who told him to stay quiet because the car was sold 'as is'. The mechanic is now being treated coldly by coworkers.
The general manager (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the situation and recommend what the dealership should do now and what it should do to build an ethical culture.
f: The car was sold for $14,200
The dealership sells 900 cars a year
The mechanic has worked there for six years
An online review mentioned 'questionable practices' last month
p: Describe the nature of ethics
Explain reasons for ethical dilemmas
Recognize and respond to ethical dilemmas
Build trust in relationships
Explain the nature of organizational culture
n: Defines ethics as principles of right and wrong that guide behavior
Explains pressure to hit sales numbers as a cause of ethical lapses
Contacts the buyer, discloses and offers a remedy
Protects the mechanic from retaliation
Sets clear standards, training and a safe way to report concerns
q: The 'as is' clause may be legal. Why does that not end the discussion?
